Invalid clears immediately. Fault active immediately. On valid rising fault increment counter (guard 65535) and shift history. Power-up initialize counter runtime history zero. Need state variables. But if we process history before update. Need no record invalid. Good.

Alarm logic:
- if NOT VALID: alarm FALSE, hold_count 0 (or holding state clear), valid_fault_prev update maybe.
- if VALID AND FAULT: alarm TRUE, hold_count := 25 (perhaps max hold). "hold each triggered alarm for at least 500ms. Keep active while fault persists." At fault clearance, after valid clear, hold 25 scans. Set a counter to 25 on valid fault. Then while fault true remains 25. When fault false and valid, if hold_count > 0? We need semantics: "Hold the alarm for the 25 valid scans following fault clearance and clear on the 26th unless a new fault occurs." So when a valid fault occurred (edge or present) we set hold counter 25. On each valid scan with no fault: decrement from 25 to 1, alarm true. On 26th? Let's count. "Hold for the 25 valid scans following fault clearance and clear on the 26th." Suppose scan t last fault true. Set count 25. At t+1 fault false: valid scan following clearance #1 => alarm true, count should maybe 24 after decrement. ... 25 scans following clearance: counts 24..0. Clear on 26th means count down from 25 to 0 across 25 valid no-fault scans, then next valid no-fault scan alarm false. Implementation:
if valid and not fault:
  if hold_count > 0 THEN alarm := TRUE; hold_count := hold_count - 1; else alarm FALSE. This yields after 25 decrements count 0, alarm true on 25th, next no-fault valid alarm false (26th). Good if count initialized 25 on valid fault. But what if fault existed for continuous many scans? Count resets 25 each fault scan. Upon first no-fault scan, decrement. Good.
What if invalid occurs during hold: clear alarm and hold_count 0.
What if new fault occurs during hold: set alarm true and count 25. New false-to-true edge increments history again. S9 says on rising new fault write timestamp etc. If fault persisted then clear then retrigger, count. Fine.
Need ensure "minimum 500 ms" with fixed 20ms: 25 scans = 500ms. Clear on 26th, yes.

Structure:

FUNCTION_BLOCK FB
VAR_INPUT
    THICKNESS_FAULT : BOOL;
...
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
...
END_VAR
VAR
    LastValidFaultSignal : BOOL;
    AlarmHoldRemaining : USINT;
    ShiftIndex : INT;
END_VAR

// Statements

IF NOT THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID THEN
    THICKNESS_ALARM := FALSE;
    AlarmHoldRemaining := 0;
    LastValidFaultSignal := FALSE;  // maybe ensure edge? If set false, next valid fault rising.
    // no counter/history/runtime changes
ELSE
    IF THICKNESS_FAULT THEN
        THICKNESS_ALARM := TRUE;
        AlarmHoldRemaining := 25;

        IF NOT LastValidFaultSignal THEN
            IF Slab_Fault_Counter < 65535 THEN
                Slab_Fault_Counter := Slab_Fault_Counter + 1;
            END_IF;

            Slab_Fault_History[0] := FaultTimestamp;
            FOR ShiftIndex := 4 TO 1 BY -1 DO
                Slab_Fault_History[ShiftIndex] := Slab_Fault_History[ShiftIndex - 1];
            END_FOR;
        END_IF;
        LastValidFaultSignal := TRUE;
    ELSE
        IF AlarmHoldRemaining > 0 THEN
            THICKNESS_ALARM := TRUE;
            AlarmHoldRemaining := AlarmHoldRemaining - 1;
        ELSE
            THICKNESS_ALARM := FALSE;
        END_IF;
        LastValidFaultSignal := FALSE;
    END_IF;
END_IF;

IF CUTTING_RUN AND THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND NOT THICKNESS_FAULT THEN
    Slab_Runtime_Accumulator := Slab_Runtime_Accumulator + 1;
END_IF;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
